correctness.rationale: For every root query (a,b), the positive surviving centers split into A={(i,a):i<a} and B={(b,j):j>b}. A subsequent query selects only the whole A, whole B, both, neither, or one center; an informative split of A or B always has a branch of size <=1. Thus each positive root fiber has Littlestone dimension <=2, implying an all-order dimension <=3. Cardinalities <=n-2 give sharp small-order upper bounds. Fully specified four- and eight-leaf trees establish ranks 2 at n=4 and 3 at n=6, and embed in all larger orders. One edge establishes n=3, and n=2 has a unique empty hypothesis. Direct adjacency replay of all tree paths passed; the independent exact minimax checker returned ranks 0,1,2,2,3,3,3,3 for n=2..9 (22,917 states), and tested the critical fiber classification for n=2..12. No finite test is treated as a universal proof.

value.rationale: Shift graphs are a canonical, genuinely natural family of triangle-free graphs of unbounded chromatic number and are explicitly central in the 2021 stable-graph literature (03C45). Their adaptive membership complexity is a separate model-theoretic/online-learning invariant not determined by their known static VC bound. The theorem gives the complete all-order online rank, sharp threshold n=6, and explicit worst-case mistake trees, demonstrating uniform adjacency-formula finite rank despite the chromatic growth. This is a structural classification with a motivated exact invariant, not a reparameterized finite computation or a routine corollary of the cited chromatic/VC results.
